question: When a neighbouring plugin hands the llm/stream wrapper a chunk it did not expect, does the turn survive, and can a repair dispatch under a name the profile already owns?
contract_after_r69: remedy may only pass a chunk through, repair a proven fusion, or rethrow the original failure; it must not raise an error of its own
measured_on: the R68 tree (plugin and engine dist as published in 0.4.18; R66–R68 moved no runtime byte)

scenarios.name: a neighbour yields null
scenarios.thrown: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')

scenarios.name: arguments is not a string
scenarios.thrown: TypeError: text.trim is not a function

scenarios.name: block-end without block
scenarios.thrown: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')

scenarios.name: the source throws
scenarios.judgement: the source error was passed through

scenarios.name: a neighbour owns remedy_unattributed
scenarios.judgement: a neighbour-owned fallback name was dispatched

limits: the harness mounts the listener directly; it does not run a host turn or a provider
the scenarios are the shapes a neighbour could produce, not a survey of installed plugins
the reserved-name row uses a synthetic profile: whether a real profile owns that name is what scan_plugin_seams.mjs answers
